verdict: Gameplay is unchanged from v2. I proved this rather than sampling it. The same scripted bots with a seeded Math.random give bit-identical per-tick player position and velocity in v2 (legacy/, three r128) and v3 (WebGL 2): the whole Act 1 route (3 checkpoints, loops, springs, dash panels, homing chains), the boss (8 hits), the capsule and results, then the whole Act 2 descent (tricks, hoops, 360° bumper orbit, flight, goal) and results. Final scores, rings, times, lives and saved records are identical. The only variation is which scattered rings get picked up, because three.js uuid generation consumes Math.random. Every Act 1 and Act 2 placement, solid, terrain/ground sample, route point and car is also identical. Real input works the same in v2, on WebGL 2 and on WebGPU: trusted CDP keyboard and mouse, the emulated Gamepad API, and phone multi-touch on the joystick, SAUT and ROULER (run, jump, homing, roll, spin dash, camera, pause menu, act chips, carve, ollie, trick, tuck). These also work: WebGPU-missing, adapter or device failure fallbacks; the French error screen with the legacy link (desktop and phone); context and GPU-process loss; missing assets and fonts; GitHub Pages sub-path /Pat3d/ including Act 2 and the legacy link; French text (new strings correct, none lost); persistence in both directions with v2; resizes and rotation on both backends; and simulation CPU cost. SPEC3 §6 draw-call and triangle budgets hold on every preset over 84 views along both whole routes (worst: Ultra 203 calls / 2.08 M tris; Moyen 160 / 683 k). Not publishable as is, because of one blocker. On WebGPU, the default backend of desktop Chrome and Edge, switching Graphismes in Act 2 Économie -> Moyen -> Économie turns the 3D view black, with a validation error every frame, until another preset is chosen. It is a one-line fix in 25-city.js. There is one major issue: Act 2 garbage of 0.6-1.5 MB per drawn frame, against 0.04 MB in v2, mostly from r186 material-cache-key rebuilds caused by the alpha-tested foliage shadow casters. There are two minor touch and pause-menu issues; the first is pre-existing in v2. Limits: all of this ran on SwiftShader in headless Chromium. Frame times, GC pauses and real-GPU or real-phone behaviour were not measured. The gamepad was the emulated Gamepad API, not hardware. Act 2 'Chargement…' on a throttled 1.6 Mbps link: the card hits its 4 s cap with city_nrm (719 KB) still loading, and the act starts with flat normals that fill in later. This was hard to see in the screenshot, so it is not reported as a finding.

findings.title: WebGPU: Act 2 renders a black 3D view after Graphismes Économie -> Moyen -> Économie (shadow map destroyed but still bound)
findings.file: src/25-city.js (applyShadows, line 3553: `if (sh.mapSize.x !== size) { sh.mapSize.set(size, size); if (sh.map) { sh.map.dispose(); sh.map = null; } }`); same pattern in src/20-world.js:799 (not reproduced in Act 1)
findings.evidence: dev/review-gameplay/shadowbreak.js (WebGPU, Act 2, real keyboard pause menu) -> dev/review-gameplay/out/shadowbreak-gpu.json. Steps: Élevé mean luma 98.3 -> Économie 98.0 -> Moyen 95.1 -> Économie again: mean 0, std 0, 1 colour, 10 x 'Uncaptured WebGPU GPUValidationError: Destroyed texture [Texture "ShadowDepthTexture"] used in a submit' per 4 frames. Still black 2 s later. Back to Élevé recovers (114.9). Screenshots: dev/review-gameplay/shots/shadowbreak-gpu-4-low-2s-later.png (black view, HUD only) vs shadowbreak-gpu-1-low.png. Act 1 with the same sequence: no error, image normal (out/shadowbreak-gpu-a1.json). A single Moyen -> Économie switch is fine (out/shadowbreak-gpu-frommedium.json). On WebGL 2 the same trigger gives 3 'WebGL: INVALID_OPERATION: bindTexture: attempt to use a deleted object' per frame without a visible change (deltex.js --act2 -> out/deltex-a2.json; lowshot2.js -> out/lowshot2-gl.json, 2nd visit vs 1st mean diff <= 1.4/255 with shadows intact). The leak run also logged them (out/leak-webgl2.json warns). Phones: by code reading, touch devices use a 1024 map for both modes, so the dispose branch is not taken; I did not run a phone WebGPU page.
findings.fix_hint: Do not dispose or null `light.shadow.map` yourself: r186's ShadowNode owns that target and resizes it when shadow.mapSize changes. Alternatively, use a separate 1024 DirectionalLight for Économie and toggle visibility, as is already done for sunS/sunC. Align 20-world.js:799. Re-run `node dev/review-gameplay/shadowbreak.js` (WebGPU, Act 2 and --act1) and `node dev/review-gameplay/deltex.js --act2` (WebGL 2): expect 0 errors and a normal mean luma at every step.

findings.title: Act 2 allocates 0.6-1.5 MB of JS garbage per drawn frame (v2: 0.04 MB), mostly r186 material cache-key rebuilds from the alpha-tested city foliage shadows
findings.evidence: dev/review-gameplay/alloc.js (CDP sampling heap profiler, objects already collected by the GC included, test-helper code excluded) -> out/alloc-webgl2.json. JS allocated per drawn frame without ticking, v2 -> v3: Act 1 55 -> 197 KB, Act 2 43 -> 1046 KB. Simulation ticks are similar: 43-54 vs 65-69 KB. dev/review-gameplay/alloc2.js -> out/alloc2-desk.json, Act 2 KB per frame: Ultra 1457, Élevé 1271, Moyen 604, Économie 620. Of that, 858 / 845 / 280 / 277 KB is under three r186 RenderObject.getMaterialCacheKey. dev/review-gameplay/cachekey.js -> out/cachekey-webgl2.json: Act 2 rebuilds about 75 cache keys per frame, all shadow-pass render objects with reason 'matVersion' (Act 1: 0.2). dev/review-gameplay/alphatest.js: the 5 'city-foliage' meshes are the only shadow casters with alphaTest > 0 (Act 1 has none). The renderer copies material.alphaTest onto the one shared shadow override material, and the Material.alphaTest setter bumps .version each time a caster crosses 0 <-> 0.5 (three r186 src/materials/Material.js:495-499 and src/renderers/common/Renderer.js about line 3748). Every later caster then fails RenderObjects' version check. SPEC3 §6 asks for no per-frame allocations in hot paths. At 60 fps this is about 36 MB/s on Moyen and 76-87 MB/s on Élevé/Ultra. GC pauses on real phones were not measured (SwiftShader only). The cache-key CPU share measured here was 0.2-0.7 % of a SwiftShader frame.
findings.fix_hint: Keep material.alphaTest at 0 on the foliage: do the cut-out with `m.alphaTestNode = float(0.5)` or a discard in the node graph. maskShadowNode already cuts the shadow. Re-run `node dev/review-gameplay/cachekey.js` (expect about 0 rebuilds per Act 2 frame) and `node dev/review-gameplay/alloc2.js` (expect cacheKeyKBPerFrame about 0, and Act 2 per-frame allocation close to Act 1's).

findings.title: Phone: the pause button ignores a tap while the other thumb holds the joystick, and a tap right after a camera swipe (pre-existing, same in v2)
findings.file: src/90-main.js wireTools (about line 1271): btnPause / btnSound listen to 'click' only
findings.evidence: dev/review-gameplay/pausetap2.js (phone 844x390, CDP touch, while playing) -> dev/review-gameplay/out/pausetap-v3.json and out/pausetap-v2.json (identical). A quick tap, or a tap held 30/120/250 ms, gives pointerdown, pointerup and click, and the game pauses. A tap while a second finger holds the joystick gives pointerdown and pointerup but no click, and the game is not paused. Chromium does not synthesise click for a non-primary touch. A tap right after a 144 px camera swipe also gives no click and no pause (fling cancel). The same tap 1.5 s after the swipe pauses.
findings.fix_hint: Act on pointerup (or pointerdown) with a pointerId check on the tool buttons, as touchButton() does for SAUT and ROULER, and keep click only for the keyboard and mouse.

findings.title: Pause menu: one tap or confirm on the new 'Version classique' row leaves the game at once (current run lost), just under 'Retour au titre', with smaller rows than v2
findings.file: src/90-main.js pauseConfirm / openLegacy (about lines 418-434) and the pause layout (PAUSE_ROWS = 5, step 30, h 25)
findings.evidence: dev/review-gameplay/touch.js -> out/touch-webgl2.json pauseRects: on the phone (844x390) the 5 rows are 30.4 px tall at a 36.5 px pitch. v2 had 4 rows of 34 px (out/touch-v2.json). Tapping a row confirms it immediately (pauseMenu: `if (i >= 0) { G.pauseSel = i; pauseConfirm(1); }`). Row 4 is `location.href = 'legacy/'`. dev/review-gameplay/subpath.js -> out/subpath.json: confirming row 4 navigated straight to /Pat3d/legacy/ (status 200, three r128) without a confirmation step.
findings.fix_hint: Ask for confirmation ('Quitter la partie ?') before openLegacy, or move 'Version classique' to the title screen or the error overlay only. Keep the pause rows at least 34 px tall on the phone.
